title: FHIR core definitions

http://hl7.org/fhir/StructureDefinition.external: FHIR StructureDefinition, published by HL7 (https://hl7.org/fhir/<release>/); a local copy is only a cache

summary: The FHIR core specification's definitions for each stable release (R4 4.0.1, R4B 4.3.0, R5 5.0.0), with HL7's publication as the authority: resources, complex and primitive datatypes and the root types, one graph per release keyed by canonical URL (http://hl7.org/fhir/StructureDefinition/<id>). A pins node names HL7's own hl7.fhir.<release>.core package at its hl7.org URL, by sha1 and sha512; a manifest per release lists every definition with HL7's published URL for it, its kind, base and the sha256 of its bytes in HL7's package; a class model per release is the UML derived from that package, which HL7 publishes only as pictures, citing the definition and element of every class and attribute.

avatar.reads: a type hierarchy in three tiers — FHIR's base types over its datatypes and resources

rationale: Owner, 2026-11-14: "fhir structured definitions and base resources etc should be loaded in fhir-harness for stable fhir releases to represent it as a harnessed KG." A kind of its own rather than a family of `fhir-artifact-index`, by the test that entry applies: different CODE, or only different RULES? An artefact index is reconstructed from ONE IG's published output, every field naming the file it came out of, and its nodes are representations of artefacts kept elsewhere. These nodes are the definitions THEMSELVES, read from a versioned package of the specification and checked against a pinned hash, and a reader resolves an element's type or a `baseDefinition` against them by canonical URL and release. Neither the writer nor the question asked of it is the index's. `derived`: `fhir-core.ts index` computes every manifest from the pinned package and none is edited; a finding against a manifest is a finding against the writer or the pin. Not `renderable`: the schema viewer reads the bodies as classes, it does not render this directory. Kept here, not in a WHO overlay, because nothing about the core specification is WHO's. Owner, 2026-11-15: "reference published hl7. assets as authoratative" and "just use fhir-harness to derived stuff (e.g. UML) that is not part of core IG publisher". So nothing here restates a definition: a reader is sent to HL7's URL, and what this layer adds is what HL7 does not publish as data, the class model. A local copy of the bodies is a cache, labelled as one in its directory (`<release>/cache/CACHE.md`), never committed, each file held to the sha256 HL7's package gave it; a mirror (the package registry) may fill the cache but is never read for a manifest or the class model. A release whose package could not be read is `status: "unread"` with no `definitions`: unread is not empty.
